amstar2_items.justification: Objectives and eligibility criteria define the population (people experiencing homelessness), policy/intervention domain (WASH and public-health pandemic responses), cross-national/jurisdictional comparison (international contexts and Brazil), and evaluative outcomes (immediate access, equity, sustainability, and effectiveness).
No a priori protocol, PROSPERO/OSF registration, or statement establishing review methods prior to conduct is reported.

Authors explicitly justify including peer-reviewed empirical/case studies alongside normative legal instruments and operational institutional guidance because pandemic responses were formulated in real time through decrees, technical briefs, and contingency plans.

Searched four databases (Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, Google Scholar) and grey/governmental repositories and listed main keywords, but did not provide reproducible database-specific Boolean strings, did not justify language restrictions (English, Portuguese, Spanish), and reported an implausibly small initial yield (95 records across four databases including Google Scholar) indicative of unstated pre-filtering.
No mention of independent duplicate screening or inter-rater agreement during document selection.
Data extraction into the four-axis matrix was described, but duplicate independent extraction or verification by a second reviewer was not reported.

Authors state that 1 of 95 retrieved documents was excluded after qualitative screening, but do not cite or identify the excluded document or provide a specific exclusion reason beyond general ineligibility.

The complete table of 94 included sources is relegated to an external supplement (Table S1), and inline Tables 2-5 only summarize illustrative policies and barriers without reporting study designs, sample sizes, or empirical methods for the 36 included peer-reviewed articles.
No risk-of-bias or methodological quality appraisal tool was used; the authors explicitly state they classified documents by analytical function rather than assessing quality or evidence hierarchy.
Funding sources for the included primary studies and reports were not extracted or reported.
Qualitative/descriptive thematic categorization and frequency counts only; no quantitative meta-analysis was performed.
No quantitative synthesis or meta-analysis was conducted.
Because no risk-of-bias or quality assessment of empirical studies was performed, study-level methodological limitations were not accounted for when interpreting findings.

Authors extensively compare and explain cross-national and subnational variations in policy implementation across institutional contexts (e.g., US decentralized municipal/privatized responses vs. Brazil's federal PNPSR/SUS/SUAS framework and municipal decrees vs. UK Everyone In).
No quantitative meta-analysis was conducted, and publication/selection bias was not investigated.
Funding support (CAPES Finance Code 001) and a conflict-of-interest declaration stating no conflicts are explicitly reported on page 13.

raw_response.methodological_notes: Self-described 'documentary and integrative review' of 94 documents (36 peer-reviewed scientific articles [38.3%], 30 institutional reports [31.9%], 20 governmental legal/regulatory decrees and plans [21.3%], and 9 technical reports/notes [9.6%]; note subcounts sum to 95 in the authors' text). Substantively, the review squarely satisfies narrow Criterion 2 by analyzing federal/state/municipal decrees (e.g., Brazil's Decree 7.053/2009 PNPSR, emergency municipal decrees), urban public-space criminalization/access rules, intergovernmental coordination, and Housing First/tenure integration governing WASH access for unhoused populations. Methodologically, however, it is a hybrid documentary-integrative policy review rather than a rigorous systematic review (Critically Low on AMSTAR 2): no protocol registration, no PRISMA diagram, no duplicate screening/extraction, no risk-of-bias assessment, and an implausible screening yield (95 records identified across Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar, with only 1 excluded to leave 94). Moreover, although eligibility criteria specified 2020-2024, pre-2020 sources (2009, 2010, 2016, 2017, 2019) are cited in the synthesis. The full inventory of 94 included documents resides in external Supplementary Material Table S1; only 35 distinct sources (16 peer-reviewed journal articles, 1 preprint, 1 book chapter, 1 IPEA survey note, and 16 governmental/institutional/media sources) are named in the text/tables and Reference list, all of which are extracted here for primary-study overlap auditing.
